tagline: An old turnpike north between the stone walls.
intro: Route 169 leaves Lisbon and runs north through Canterbury, Brooklyn, Pomfret and Woodstock to the Massachusetts line along the old line of the Norwich and Woodstock Turnpike, a toll road incorporated in 1801. It keeps company with the Quinebaug River for a while without ever quite meeting it. Stone walls line the fields, and glacial boulders lie strewn among them between stands of maple and pine.

In Pomfret the road becomes Pomfret Street, two miles of old houses and two private schools. Woodstock was a farm town, then a mill town, and when the mills went quiet it turned into a summer place for wealthy city families.

moments.title: Prudence Crandall Museum, Canterbury
moments.text: On the village green stands the house where Prudence Crandall reopened her school for Black girls in 1833. Violence closed it the next year. The state later named her its official heroine.

moments.title: Brooklyn
moments.text: General Israel Putnam sits his horse just south of the green, his sarcophagus set into the pedestal after too many visitors called at his old tomb.

moments.title: Roseland Cottage, Woodstock
moments.text: Henry Bowen's coral-pink Gothic summer house of 1846, where four presidents came to speak on the Fourth of July and the nation's oldest surviving indoor bowling alley still keeps its lanes.
